classes.name: Stakeholder
classes.description: An entity (organization or role) that participates in business activities and receives value through the system or service being developed.

classes.name: Value
classes.description: Represents the benefits or desired states that stakeholders gain through the system or service being developed.
extract_rules: Extract Value when the text explicitly describes a stakeholder-focused benefit or desired end-state that stakeholders gain from the system or service.

Extract Value when the statement expresses an improvement or outcome that is attributable to the system and is phrased in terms of stakeholder impact (for example, phrases such as "reduce time to", "increase accuracy of", "improve customer satisfaction", "reduce cost for", or "increase revenue from").

Extract Value when the benefit includes an identifiable beneficiary (e.g., customers, users, operators, business units) and, where available, an associated measure or qualitative descriptor of the improvement (e.g., time, accuracy, satisfaction, cost, revenue, risk).

Extract Value only when the content describes outcomes or end-states rather than solutions, capabilities, actions, or technical implementations; if the statement describes a capability, activity, feature, or system requirement, map it to Feature, Business Activity, or System Requirement instead of Value.

Extract Value statements even when phrased qualitatively, provided they are clearly framed as stakeholder benefits or desired end-states (for example, "better decision-making for managers" or "faster incident resolution for customers").

Extract Value when the statement frames a stakeholder benefit, outcome, or desired end-state and includes explicit outcome-framing or trigger words such as "benefit", "value", "improve", "reduce", "increase", "enable", or similar verbs indicating positive change; do not extract statements that only describe means, features, or system capabilities without outcome framing.
Extract only tangible outcomes or benefits; do not extract abstract concepts or process steps as Values, and if a candidate describes a process, re-classify it as a Business Activity.
Extract only qualitative or quantitative benefits, outcomes, or improvements; do not extract process steps, activities, or system capabilities, as these belong to Business Activity or Feature.

classes.name: Vision
classes.description: A statement that concisely expresses the long-term ideal state that a company, business, or project aims to achieve.
extract_rules: Extract only high-level strategic objectives or aspirational statements that define the long-term ideal state of the entity.

classes.name: Concept
classes.description: A statement that concisely expresses the activity policy toward realizing the ideal (vision) of a company, business, or project.
extract_rules: Extract a Concept when the text describes a high-level domain idea, taxonomy, policy, framework, or other conceptual notion that captures the intended vision or guiding approach (for example: "risk model", "triage protocol", "fraud detection concept").
Extract a Concept only when the phrase denotes an abstract construct or organizing principle rather than a concrete action, task, or named product/feature.
When a phrase describes an ability, capability, or a concrete mechanism (for example: a specific feature, step, or action), prefer extracting it as Feature or Business Activity instead of Concept.

If a candidate Concept is a short noun phrase that could be interpreted either as an abstract notion or as a concrete item, extract it and flag it for consolidation review to determine correct abstraction layer and linkage to Feature or Business Activity entries.

Include contextual qualifiers or definitions when available (for example, brief description or intended outcome) to confirm that the extracted item functions as a conceptual policy or framework rather than a concrete task.

Extract only domain-specific entities or terminology, prioritizing them over generic process descriptions or common nouns; if a candidate is better described as a Feature or System Requirement, prioritize those classes over Concept.

classes.name: Business Activity
classes.description: A business activity performed by stakeholders; business requirements are realized through these activities.
extract_rules: Extract a Business Activity only when the phrase describes a process, task, or operation performed by an actor; prefer verbs, gerunds, or process nouns that imply action, and do not extract single-word outcomes, goals, or metrics (map those to Value or Indicator).

Extract a Business Activity when the phrase is a verb or verb phrase that denotes a repeatable operation or end-to-end business process performed by an actor or stakeholder (for example: "process payments", "onboard customers", "schedule appointments").

Extract a Business Activity when the described operation delivers observable business value or outcome and can be executed or repeated by a person, role, or organizational unit rather than being an internal implementation detail.

Extract a Business Activity when the phrase names a cohesive task or workflow (one or more steps) that stakeholders recognize as a business-level responsibility, even if it can be decomposed into subtasks.
Extract a Business Activity when the phrase explicitly or implicitly identifies the performing actor (role, team, or external stakeholder) or when actor attribution is inferable from context.
Extract a Business Activity when the phrase expresses a recurring or regularized function of the business (scheduled, periodic, or standard operating procedures) rather than a one-off event.

Extract as Business Activity only processes, workflows, or actions performed by stakeholders; exclude static objects, data entities, or system outputs, and ensure the activity describes a dynamic process with a clear purpose.

Extract only activities that involve a clear transformation of input to output or a specific operational process; exclude high-level strategic objectives or vague business intentions to prevent scope creep.
prohibit_rules: Do not accept candidates that are static states, goals, or desired outcomes; these belong to Value or Business Requirement, as a Business Activity must involve a verb-based process or operational execution.

Do not extract as Business Activity if the entity describes a technical system capability, a specific feature, or a static system requirement; Business Activities must represent high-level organizational processes, operational tasks, or workflows.

Do not extract activities that are purely technical, internal system processes, or administrative tasks (e.g., "data logging", "system initialization"); these should be excluded or mapped to System Component functionality.

Do not extract high-level strategic objectives or mission statements as Business Activity; these should be categorized as Vision or Analysis Goal, as a Business Activity must represent a specific, repeatable operational process.

classes.name: Business Requirement
classes.description: Descriptions of business requirements demanded of the system or service being developed.
extract_rules: Extract a Business Requirement when the text contains obligative or modal verbs that indicate a prescriptive demand, such as "shall", "must", "required", "should", "will", or explicit phrases like "is required to" or "is required that".

Extract a Business Requirement when the sentence follows a stakeholder-driven need structure: [Stakeholder] + [verb of need/obligation] + [action or outcome], for example "The user must be able to..." or "The department shall ensure...".
Extract a Business Requirement when the text defines a constraint, obligation, acceptance criterion, or a mandated capability that implies a change to system behavior, process, or deliverable.

Extract a Business Requirement when the statement includes measurable or testable criteria (e.g., performance thresholds, deadlines, success conditions) that indicate a requirement rather than a high-level goal.

When extracting, capture and attach an evidence token list containing the obligative/modal verbs and key phrases found in the source text (for example: "shall", "must", "required", "should", "is required to", "is required that", "must be able to", "shall ensure").
Extract a Business Requirement when the statement is explicitly labeled or introduced as a requirement (for example: headings, bullets, or prefatory text like "Business Requirement:").

If the text is outcome-oriented but lacks prescriptive language or obligative verbs (for example, it describes a desired outcome, goal, or benefit such as "improve customer satisfaction"), treat it as a Value rather than a Business Requirement and do not extract it as a Business Requirement.

Extract candidate Business Requirements even when conditional language is present (for example "If X, the system must..."), but include the condition text and evidence tokens so a reviewer can confirm scope and applicability.

Extract a Business Requirement when the text describes a clear stakeholder pain point or operational friction that necessitates a system solution, even if explicit obligative language is absent, provided the context implies a mandatory corrective action.

Ensure extracted Business Requirements are phrased as actionable needs (e.g., "The system must allow X"). If a candidate is phrased as a noun-heavy concept without an action, re-evaluate if it should be a Concept instead.

Prefer Business Requirement only when the statement expresses a business need, obligation, policy, or operational outcome at the problem level; if the sentence mainly names a concrete function such as notifying, displaying, recording, deleting, inputting, or guiding, re-evaluate it as Feature or System Requirement.

Keep the candidate as Business Requirement when the sentence describes an organizational, service-operation, governance, documentation, support, or compliance obligation (for example preparing FAQs, providing support arrangements, maintaining documentation, or ensuring operational continuity), even if action verbs are present.
prohibit_rules: Do not extract as a Business Requirement if the text describes a technical implementation detail or a specific UI element; these should be captured as Feature or System Component.

Do not extract as Business Requirement if the content describes a static system component, a technical feature implementation, or a data entity. Requirements must focus on business needs, outcomes, or constraints, not technical solutions.

Do not extract as Business Requirement when the candidate is dominated by concrete system behavior or interface action verbs such as notify, display, input, record, delete, send, guide, or show and the sentence reads like a functional behavior specification rather than a business need.

Do not extract as Business Requirement when the sentence primarily specifies a user-facing function, screen behavior, control flow, or data-handling operation that could directly map to a Feature or System Requirement.
Do not reject a candidate as Business Requirement solely because it contains action verbs if the action is primarily organizational or service-operational rather than a concrete system function.

classes.name: Feedback
classes.description: Feedback produced from analytical insights by the data analysis.

classes.name: Analysis Goal
classes.description: The purpose of data analysis; it leads to analytical insights and is defined by indicators.

classes.name: Analytical Insight
classes.description: An insight derived from data analysis that contributes to designing business values.

classes.name: Indicator
classes.description: A metric/indicator used to define analysis goals and estimated by analytical insights.

classes.name: Operational Data
classes.description: Operational data produced by system components and interfaces (e.g., logs, events, usage records).
extract_rules: When extracting Operational Data instances, prefer noun phrases that denote concrete, measurable data artifacts such as logs, telemetry, events, sensor readings, dataset names, usage records, and audit trails.

Mark phrases that explicitly include collection attributes (source, collection frequency, format, protocol, or location) — for example, 'API logs', 'sensor readings at 1Hz', 'Kafka event stream', or 'CSV export from billing system' — as strong candidates for Operational Data.

If a candidate phrase names a data artifact but lacks explicit collection attributes (for example, 'application logs' without source or frequency), tag it as a candidate-level Operational Data instance with lower confidence and capture missing provenance details where possible.

Include Operational Data mentions that convey structural or operational properties relevant to extraction, such as schema names, event types, timestamp conventions, retention policy references, partitioning keys, sampling rates, and storage locations.

Prefer extraction of names or identifiers of datasets, log streams, and event channels (for example, 'transaction_log_2024', 'error_event_stream', 'sensor_temperature_readings') rather than high-level conceptual descriptions.
When available, extract Operational Data together with contextual metadata (source system, collection method, frequency, and format) to support unambiguous classification and downstream usage.

classes.name: External Data
classes.description: External data obtained from outside the system/organization (e.g., market data, third-party datasets).

classes.name: Research Data
classes.description: Research/experimental data related to business activities (e.g., surveys, studies, experiment results).

classes.name: System Requirement
classes.description: Descriptions of technical specifications for the system or service being developed.
extract_rules: Extract requirements only if they specify a functional capability, performance constraint, security/privacy constraint, data-handling rule, retention rule, interface specification, or other verifiable technical behavior.

Extract a System Requirement when the statement defines how the system must behave, what technical constraint it must satisfy, or what data/security/performance condition it must enforce, even if phrased as a full requirement sentence rather than a short feature label.

Prefer System Requirement over Business Requirement when the statement is testable at the system level and focuses on implementation-neutral technical behavior or constraint rather than business motivation.

Prefer System Requirement for retention, privacy, security, performance, interface, and data-handling rules only when the text constrains the system's technical behavior rather than assigning an organizational or service-operation responsibility.
prohibit_rules: Do not extract high-level business goals or vague aspirations as System Requirement; these should be categorized as Value or Business Requirement instead.
Only extract requirements that define specific system behaviors, interfaces, or functional constraints.

Do not extract as System Requirement if the entity describes a broad business goal, a business process, or an organizational strategy; System Requirements must be verifiable, technical specifications, constraints, or functional capabilities of the system.

Do not extract as System Requirement when the candidate is merely a short user-facing capability label or product feature name without a requirement statement, constraint, or technical condition; classify such cases as Feature instead.

Do not reject a candidate as System Requirement solely because it mentions user-visible behavior if the sentence still specifies a verifiable system rule, limit, retention policy, security condition, or technical handling constraint.

Do not extract as System Requirement when the statement is primarily about organizational support, documentation, service-operation arrangements, governance, or operational responsibility assignment rather than a technical rule that the system itself must satisfy.

classes.name: Feature
classes.description: A user/system-facing capability that realizes system requirements and is implemented by system components.
extract_rules: Extract a Feature when the text explicitly names a user-facing capability or product feature using terms such as "feature", "capability", "function", "option", "module" (when used in a user-facing sense), or other wording that indicates functionality delivered to end users.

Extract a Feature when the description emphasizes user interactions, UI/UX elements, user goals, or intended user benefits (for example: screens, buttons, workflows, user stories, or phrases like "users can", "allows users to", "provides users with").

Extract the canonical name or label of the Feature as presented in the source (e.g., feature name, menu/option label, or marketing name) when available, and extract a concise one-sentence description of the Feature's purpose or user outcome.
Extract Feature-level acceptance criteria, user-facing constraints, and typical user scenarios when they are clearly associated with the named capability.
When source text pairs features with business or product requirements (goals, KPIs, value proposition), extract those associations as attributes of the Feature.

Prefer extracting a System Component or Interface (not Feature) when the text refers to explicit implementation artifacts such as modules, services, APIs, databases, servers, hardware, libraries, classes, code-level components, or deployment infrastructure.

If a phrase is ambiguous between being a user-facing capability and an implementation artifact, extract both the Feature and the System Component and tag the extraction with the label "feature/component ambiguous" to signal the need for later consolidation and review.
Extract Feature-level relationships to other Features (dependencies, enabled-by, supersedes) when the relationships are expressed in user-facing or product-oriented terms.
Extract features described in marketing, documentation, or product roadmaps when they describe user-facing capabilities, even if implementation details are also included in the same source.
prohibit_rules: Do not extract abstract goals, strategic intents, or high-level outcomes as Features; Features must be concrete, deliverable functionalities, so reject any candidate that represents an abstract concept or a long-term goal.

classes.name: Interface
classes.description: An interface exposed by system components and/or features; it can produce operational data.
extract_rules: Extract an Interface when the text explicitly identifies an interaction point or channel through which a system component or feature exposes functionality (for example: API, endpoint, user interface, web portal, REST call, SOAP service, UI screen, or CLI).

Extract an Interface when the description indicates a concrete integration touchpoint between systems or a concrete interaction point between a user and a system (for example: 'payment gateway endpoint', 'mobile app login screen', 'order submission API').

Extract an Interface when it describes the mechanism that accepts requests or provides responses, publishes events, or defines a callable contract (for example: endpoints that accept HTTP requests, message topics, callbacks, or published service operations).

Extract an Interface when it is tied to an implementation or operational artifact (for example: documented endpoints, URLs, ports, SDKs, service endpoints) rather than abstract organizational functions or roles.

When the text primarily describes the data being exchanged, the message content, or the schema/payload (rather than the channel or interaction point itself), extract Operational Data instead of extracting an Interface.

Extract Interfaces only when the reference is concrete and actionable (identifiers, protocol, URL, method, endpoint name, or UI screen name); do not extract ambiguous or purely conceptual mentions unless additional context clarifies an actual interaction point.

classes.name: System Component
classes.description: Descriptions of modules and libraries that make up the system or service being developed.

properties.name: hasConcept
properties.description: Associates concepts linked to a vision.
prohibit_rules: Do not extract hasConcept when the candidate span is a verb or verb phrase or otherwise clearly procedural or action-oriented (describing steps, actions, or processes).
Do not extract hasConcept when the candidate span expresses temporal information such as dates, durations, timelines, scheduling, or sequence markers.
Do not extract hasConcept when the candidate span denotes an outcome, result, benefit, metric, value judgment, or measurable effect rather than an abstract idea or conceptual entity.

Do not extract hasConcept when the candidate span is not a definitional noun phrase describing an abstract idea (for example, single-word fragments, isolated entities without conceptual description, or mere labels without definitional context).

Do not extract hasConcept when there are no explicit concept-linking cues in the local context (for example, phrases like "concept of", "notion", "term", "defined as", "refers to", or similar phrasing); absence of such cues should prevent extraction.

Do not extract hasConcept when the target is a verb phrase, procedural description, or otherwise ambiguous between an action/entity and a concept; only accept hasConcept when the target is a clearly conceptual noun phrase (definitions, terms, metaphors). For ambiguous mappings, do not extract unless there is an explicit concept-linking cue in the local context (for example, "concept of", "idea of", "term", "notion", "defined as", or similar).

properties.name: realizeValue
properties.description: Associates the value that a concept realizes.
prohibit_rules: Do not create a realizeValue relation when the source is not a Concept or when the destination is not a Value-like outcome, benefit, or desired end state.

Do not accept realizeValue candidates that are only implied by document proximity or loose thematic similarity between a Concept and a Value when no local causal, enabling, or realization language is present in the text.

Do not create realizeValue relations from phrasing that is clearly aspirational, speculative, or promotional (for example, uses formulations such as "aims to", "intends to", "plans to", "hopes to", "could", or similar) unless the text explicitly links the Concept as enabling, delivering, or realizing the Value.
Do not infer realizeValue from generic statements about a system, policy, or concept unless the local context shows that the named Concept contributes to or explains how the Value is achieved.

properties.name: receivesValue
properties.description: Associates the value that a stakeholder receives.

properties.name: participates
properties.description: Associates business activities in which a stakeholder participates.
prohibit_rules: Do not extract a 'participates' relation when either the candidate source or target is a Value, Vision, Principle, Goal, or other conceptual/abstract class rather than an Agent-like class (e.g., Stakeholder, Role, Organization, System Component) paired with an Activity or Event class.

Do not extract a 'participates' relation if the candidate does not link an Agent-like entity to an Activity or Event; participation must represent an agent performing, attending, executing, or otherwise engaging in an activity or event.

Do not extract a 'participates' relation when the supporting text uses only aspirational, hypothetical, or goal-oriented language (for example, includes phrases such as "aims to", "seeks to", "plans to", "supports the goal of", or similar) without explicit wording that an identified agent actually performs or participates in the activity.

Do not extract a 'participates' relation when the candidate evidence describes responsibilities, intentions, or capabilities in a way that does not indicate actual involvement (for example, descriptions of responsibility, eligibility, or potential role without clear participation behavior).

properties.name: hasBusinessRequirement
properties.description: Associates business requirements linked to a value.
prohibit_rules: Do not create hasBusinessRequirement relations when the candidate requirement describes an implementation detail, feature, task, or specific action rather than a business need.

Do not accept a hasBusinessRequirement relation if the target label contains verbs that describe system behavior (for example, "send", "store", "calculate", "authenticate") or contains technical nouns or artifacts (for example, "API", "database", "server", "endpoint"); instead surface the candidate as a Feature or System Requirement.

Do not map items as business requirements when the text encodes technical constraints, specific technologies, configuration steps, or UI/UX implementation notes; classify these as implementation or solution-level artifacts rather than business-level requirements.

properties.name: realizedBy
properties.description: Associates the business activity by which a business requirement is realized.
prohibit_rules: Do not accept a realizedBy relation when the target is an abstract Concept or a generic Business Activity unless the source text contains explicit implementation/realization wording (for example, 'realized by', 'implemented by', 'provided by').

Do not accept a realizedBy relation that links a business Goal, Value, or high-level Requirement directly to a Concept or Activity described only at an abstract or conceptual level; such mappings should be marked REVIEW unless a concrete, named implementer is specified.

Do not accept a realizedBy relation when the target is a generic term (for example 'process', 'capability', 'activity') without a specific, named System Component, Feature, or implementation artifact; require a named implementer to treat the relation as valid.
Do not accept realizedBy relations where the target is a non-implementing artifact (for example 'principle', 'constraint', 'guideline') because these do not represent implementation agents.

Do not accept realizedBy relations when the connecting wording does not indicate realization/implementation (for example only 'related to' or 'supports'); mark such cases REVIEW rather than mapping them as realizedBy.

Do not use realizedBy to link a Value to a Feature; this relationship is reserved for linking Business Requirements or System Requirements to a System Component or Feature, and any Value linked to a Feature should be flagged for review.

properties.name: targetsValue
properties.description: Associates the value that this feedback targets (directly).

properties.name: targetsBusinessRequirement
properties.description: Associates the business requirement that this feedback targets (directly).

properties.name: targetsSystemRequirement
properties.description: Associates the system requirement that this feedback targets (directly).

properties.name: producesInsight
properties.description: Associates analytical insights produced from feedback.

properties.name: leadsTo
properties.description: Associates analytical insights that an analysis goal leads to.

properties.name: definedBy
properties.description: Associates indicators that define an analysis goal.

properties.name: estimates
properties.description: Associates indicators estimated by an analytical insight.

properties.name: usesOperationalData
properties.description: Associates operational data used by an analytical insight.
prohibit_rules: Do not reject or mark as prohibited usesOperationalData when the text describes routine, intended, or actual consumption of operational data such as telemetry, logs, metrics, sensor feeds, or streaming operational events.
Do not prohibit usesOperationalData based solely on vague or generic mentions of data consumption; only prohibit when the text explicitly states that operational data is NOT used.

Do not assign a prohibition when the text refers to usage of data for operational purposes unless it explicitly refers to non-operational datasets (for example, research-only, archival-only, or synthetic datasets) or otherwise disclaims operational usage.

Do not mark usesOperationalData as prohibited when the subject is clearly a data consumer or system component that consumes data; prohibit only when the entity described is not a data consumer (for example, an abstract Value, a conceptual metric with no data flow, or a purely theoretical construct) and the text explicitly indicates lack of data consumption.

Do not mark a candidate usesOperationalData relation as valid when the destination is not an explicit data artifact (for example, a sensor reading, log file, dataset, metric, event stream, or similar concrete data object); prohibit relations that point to abstract destinations.

Do not accept usesOperationalData when the phrasing indicates a conceptual discussion, mention, or description of data in the abstract (for example, 'discusses data', 'mentions metrics', 'describes a vision for data use') without explicit indication of actual data usage.

Do not accept usesOperationalData when the destination is a Business Activity, Vision, Value, goal, or other strategic/artifactual concept rather than a concrete data artifact; prohibit relations that conflate business concepts with operational data objects.

Do not accept usesOperationalData unless the text includes explicit data-usage verbs or actions (for example, 'collect', 'record', 'measure', 'log', 'ingest', 'query', 'stream', 'capture', 'monitor'); prohibit candidate relations based solely on passive or non-actionable wording.

properties.name: usesResearchData
properties.description: Associates research data used by an analytical insight.
prohibit_rules: Do not assign usesResearchData to statements that refer solely to operational telemetry, system logs, transaction records, live production metrics, or other operational/production monitoring data unless the text also explicitly describes research methodology, experimental design, data sampling, or analytic procedures that indicate use in a research or analytical study.

Do not accept usesResearchData when the origin of the data is described using phrases such as "system logs", "transaction records", "live data", "production metrics", "operational telemetry", or similar operational descriptors; such sources should be mapped to Operational Data or equivalent operational-data properties instead.

Do not mark routine business records, production databases, or operational monitoring streams as usesResearchData when they are mentioned in an operational, reporting, or monitoring context without any indication that the data were used for research, hypothesis testing, or a formal analytical study.

Avoid inferring usesResearchData from passing references to datasets or metrics where the text does not describe research intent, analytic hypotheses, study parameters, or research-specific processing steps (for example, mention of a log file used for debugging or a metrics dashboard used for operations).

properties.name: usesExternalData
properties.description: Associates external data used by an analytical insight.

properties.name: hasSystemRequirement
properties.description: Associates system requirements linked to a business requirement.
prohibit_rules: Do not link System Requirements to Business Activities directly. System Requirements must be linked to Features or System Components. If a relationship implies a dependency on an activity, re-evaluate if it should be a Business Requirement or a Business Activity.

Do not extract hasSystemRequirement if the target System Requirement is a high-level goal rather than a specific functional or non-functional requirement; ensure the relationship links specific system capabilities to concrete requirements.

properties.name: realizedByFeature
properties.description: Associates features by which a system requirement is realized.
prohibit_rules: Do not extract realizedByFeature when the candidate mapping links a high-level goal, value, or stakeholder need to a named feature unless the source text explicitly states that the feature realizes, implements, provides, or realizes the goal using clear phrases such as "implemented by feature X", "realized through feature X", or "feature X provides".

Do not accept realizedByFeature when the text only lists possible solutions, design options, or feature candidates without an explicit statement of realization; treat these cases as REVIEW rather than ACCEPT.

Do not extract realizedByFeature when the relationship is expressed speculatively or conditionally (for example, using words like "may", "might", "could", "if") unless the text also contains explicit implementation/realization wording as required by the first rule.

properties.name: implementedBy
properties.description: Associates system components that implement a feature.
prohibit_rules: Do not create implementedBy relationships when the source is a Business Activity, Value, Stakeholder, or other non-feature concept and the target is a Feature or System Component.

Do not treat phrasing that implies responsibility, ownership, benefit, or loose association (for example "used by", "owned by", "for", or "supports") as an implementedBy relationship when the text does not show that the target component executes, stores, renders, manages, or otherwise realizes the feature behavior.

Do not infer implementedBy from passive or ambiguous constructions (for example "is provided to", "is for", "is used in") when the surrounding text lacks concrete technical decomposition or allocation to the target component or layer; explicit implementation verbs are strong evidence but not mandatory if the technical role is clear.

properties.name: exposedBy
properties.description: Associates interfaces exposed by a feature.

properties.name: exposes
properties.description: Associates interfaces exposed by a system component.
prohibit_rules: Do not use 'exposes' for internal system logic or private data structures; this property is strictly reserved for external-facing interfaces or data explicitly made available to users or other systems.

properties.name: producesOperationalData
properties.description: Associates operational data produced by a system component.
prohibit_rules: Do not accept producesOperationalData assertions when the source of production is a Stakeholder, Vision, or Business Activity; such sources do not qualify as operational data producers.
Do not accept producesOperationalData unless the stated source is a System Component, Interface, or Feature; if the source is any other model element, reject the assertion.

Do not accept producesOperationalData when the text provides no concrete indication that the source component creates, records, stores, returns, transmits, computes, or otherwise handles the destination as a runtime or system-level data artifact.

Do not accept producesOperationalData unless the object is an explicit data artifact (for example: log entries, telemetry stream, sensor readings, event records, or a named data file/schema); reject assertions where the object is a vague activity, requirement, or non-data concept.

Do not accept producesOperationalData when production is described only as a manual action, business process outcome, or stakeholder deliverable; production must be characterized as system-level or runtime data generation.

Do not reject producesOperationalData solely because the text lacks explicit verbs such as "generates" or "logs" if the local context clearly allocates the named data artifact to the source component through recording, storage, transmission, computation, or interface response behavior.

properties.name: interfaceProducesOperationalData
properties.description: Associates operational data produced by an interface.
prohibit_rules: Do not extract an interfaceProducesOperationalData relation when the interface is not explicitly named or otherwise clearly identified in the source text.

Do not extract an interfaceProducesOperationalData relation when the verb phrase is metaphorical or vague (for example, 'enables insights', 'supports visibility', 'helps analyze') rather than explicitly indicating production of a data artifact.

Do not extract an interfaceProducesOperationalData relation when the source text does not connect the interface to a concrete data artifact through output, return, display, download, export, logging, or similar interface-level data delivery behavior.
If the source text names both the interface and a concrete data artifact but the production wording is indirect or weak, mark the candidate relation for REVIEW rather than rejecting it automatically.

properties.name: producesResearchData
properties.description: Associates research data produced by a business activity.
prohibit_rules: Do not mark a relation as producesResearchData when the text refers to general data, business metrics, or high-level insights rather than formal research outputs.

Do not mark a relation as producesResearchData unless the text explicitly uses research-oriented terminology such as "study", "survey", "experiment", "research data", "clinical trial", or similar phrases indicating primary or formal research.

Do not mark a relation as producesResearchData unless the text explicitly identifies research roles or agents (for example, "research team", "researchers", "principal investigator", or named academic units) that performed or produced the research.

Do not mark a relation as producesResearchData when the described work is clearly operational, analytics, or internal reporting (for example, dashboards, KPIs, operational metrics); instead, map such cases to producesOperationalData or producesInsight as appropriate.

Do not mark a relation as producesResearchData when the source is opinion-based content, anecdotal observations, vendor marketing materials, or secondary summaries (for example, press releases or market reports) that do not describe primary research methods or outputs.
